newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan oil monopoly still game for Vietnam project.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan oil monopoly still game for Vietnam project.

text.p: Taiwan's state monopoly Chinese Petroleum Corp said on Thursday it has not received any notice that Vietnam has decided to reject foreign partners and go alone in a refinery project.
"I first heard of this rumour about two weeks ago, but so far we haven't received the formal announcement from the Vietnam side," company spokeswoman Ho Li-chun told Reuters.
The $1.6 billion Dung Quat oil refinery, which will have a capacity of 6.5 million tonnes per year, is to be built in the central province of Quang Ngai.
"We have submitted our proposal (to the Vietamese government), but if it cannot commit to our requirements, we will not do it," Ho said by telephone.

"Our principle is to have at least a nine percent annual investment return from the project," she said. "And in fact, foreign banks will not approve any syndicated loan to the project if the investment return is smaller than 10-12 percent."
Ho said she doubted the Vietnam side could launch the project alone.
"Without foreign funds' support, I doubt that the cash-stricken Vietnam can do the project alone," Ho said.

In 1996, Chinese Petroleum said it would continue the refinery investment in Vietnam despite a decision to freeze overseas investments temporarily in response to an Economics Ministry call to strengthen local investments.
Chinese Petroleum and Chinese Investment Development Corp would share 10 percent of the foreign consortium in the project.

Other partners include PetroVietnam with a 30 percent stake, South Korea's LG Group with 27 percent, Stone & Webster with three percent, and Malaysia's Petronas and U.S.-based Conoco with a combined 30 percent.
